scenarioName: Septic Shock — Nursing Home Fever with Altered Mental Status

scenarioStory.history: Nursing home staff report the patient has been increasingly confused and lethargic over the past 24 hours, with poor oral intake. Found this morning with a fever of 102.9°F, low blood pressure on facility vitals, and new urinary incontinence. No witnessed trauma or fall.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 75-year-old male nursing home resident in bed, flushed, diaphoretic, and confused. Facility staff report new fever and hypotension over the past several hours. → IV/IO access and fluids started promptly: Crew obtains full vital signs and monitoring, checks blood glucose, establishes IV/IO access, and begins rapid isotonic fluid boluses toward a MAP goal while notifying the receiving hospital. → MAP remains below 65 after fluids: Fluid-refractory septic shock is recognized. Crew starts a norepinephrine infusion titrated to a MAP goal of 65 mmHg while continuing reassessment. → MAP improves, patient more alert: Perfusion and mental status are trending in the right direction with fluids and titrated norepinephrine. Patient is packaged, monitored, and transported to an appropriate facility with continued sepsis-pathway notification.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Altered mental status and fever, reported by nursing home staff

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 75-year-old male nursing home resident in bed, flushed, diaphoretic, and confused. Facility staff report new fever and hypotension over the past several hours.

scenarioEvents.name: IV/IO access and fluids started promptly
scenarioEvents.description: Crew obtains full vital signs and monitoring, checks blood glucose, establishes IV/IO access, and begins rapid isotonic fluid boluses toward a MAP goal while notifying the receiving hospital.
relatedChecklist: Obtain full vital signs, cardiac monitor, pulse oximetry, and EtCO2
Check blood glucose; correct only if less than 60 mg/dL
Establish IV access; place IO if unsuccessful within 2 attempts or 90 seconds
IV/IO fluid bolus 500 mL NS pressure-infused <15 min; repeat toward 78 kg × 30 mL/kg = 2,340 mL goal or MAP 65
Provide advance notification to receiving hospital of suspected septic shock

scenarioEvents.name: MAP remains below 65 after fluids
scenarioEvents.description: Fluid-refractory septic shock is recognized. Crew starts a norepinephrine infusion titrated to a MAP goal of 65 mmHg while continuing reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Norepinephrine infusion 8 mcg/min IV (78 kg × 0.1 mcg/kg/min), titrate to MAP ≥65 mmHg
Reassess full vital signs and mental status at least every 15 minutes

scenarioEvents.name: MAP improves, patient more alert
scenarioEvents.description: Perfusion and mental status are trending in the right direction with fluids and titrated norepinephrine. Patient is packaged, monitored, and transported to an appropriate facility with continued sepsis-pathway notification.
relatedChecklist: Continue reassessment and transport with advance notification to sepsis-capable facility

scenarioEvents.name: IV access and fluids delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Vascular access and fluid resuscitation are delayed despite obvious signs of septic shock. Perfusion continues to deteriorate: mental status worsens, blood pressure drops further, and skin signs begin transitioning toward late-stage shock.
relatedChecklist: Recognize decompensated shock; immediately obtain IV/IO access and begin rapid fluid resuscitation
